findings.title: UnixFileLock truncating open follows symlinks, zeroing arbitrary files (CVE-2025-68146)
findings.evidence: UnixFileLock._acquire builds open_flags = os.O_RDWR | os.O_TRUNC (line 41) and only appends os.O_CREAT when Path(self.lock_file).exists() is false (lines 42-43), then calls os.open(self.lock_file, open_flags, self._context.mode) (line 44) with no O_NOFOLLOW. os.open resolves symbolic links, so a symlink planted at the lock path is followed and the O_TRUNC open zeroes the link target to 0 bytes; a dangling symlink is worse: exists() returns false, O_CREAT is added, and the open creates the target file at the attacker-chosen path. Line 46 then os.fchmod()s that file to the lock mode. An attacker with write access to the directory containing a predictable lock path (e.g. /tmp/app.lock or any shared/world-writable lock directory) either pre-plants the symlink or wins the TOCTOU race between the line-42 exists() check and the line-44 open; every subsequent FileLock(...) / with lock.acquire() call by the victim destroys the targeted file. FileLock resolves to UnixFileLock on POSIX when fcntl is available (filelock/__init__.py:36-39) and AsyncUnixFileLock inherits the same _acquire (filelock/asyncio.py:330), so this is the default acquire path. Upstream fixed this in 3.20.1 by adding O_NOFOLLOW (open fails with ELOOP on a symlink).

findings.title: WindowsFileLock truncating open follows symlinks/junctions to arbitrary files (CVE-2025-68146)
findings.evidence: WindowsFileLock._acquire always opens with os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC (lines 22-26) via os.open(self.lock_file, flags, self._context.mode) (line 28). The preceding guard raise_on_not_writable_file() (line 20) is only os.stat, which follows links and does not reject a reparse point, and Windows os.open offers no O_NOFOLLOW protection, so the truncating open follows a symlink/junction planted at the lock path and zeroes the target file (or creates a missing target, since O_CREAT is always set). Precondition: local write access to the directory holding a predictable lock path plus symlink-creation ability (Developer Mode on Windows 10+), with the same check-to-open TOCTOU window as the Unix path. Fixed upstream in 3.20.1 by rejecting files with FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT via GetFileAttributesW before opening.

findings.title: SoftFileLock TOCTOU between writability check and exclusive open allows symlink swap (CVE-2026-22701)
findings.evidence: SoftFileLock._acquire calls raise_on_not_writable_file(self.lock_file) (line 17), which os.stat()s the path (following symlinks), and then opens it at line 27 with os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_TRUNC (lines 20-25). An attacker with symlink-creation rights in the lock directory can swap the path for a symlink inside the check-to-open window: if the symlink target is read-only the pre-check raises PermissionError for the victim, and if it exists (or is dangling) O_CREAT|O_EXCL fails with EEXIST on POSIX, which lines 28-33 misclassify as 'lock already exists' so acquire() polls and, with the default timeout of -1 (filelock/_api.py:311-312, 336-344), blocks indefinitely - a silent lock-acquire failure / denial of service; on implementations where exclusive-create still follows the link the lock itself is created on an unintended target. Upstream rated this Moderate (CVSS 5.3) and fixed it in 3.20.3 by adding O_NOFOLLOW to this open. Note O_EXCL prevents target truncation through this path on mainstream POSIX/Windows, so the reachable impact is lock-state confusion/DoS rather than file destruction.
